page: Microsoft Azure FX8-4ms_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the FXmsv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). It is equipped with 168.0 GB of system memory, yielding an exceptionally high resource density of 42.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, though it is premium storage capable, and it does not include any GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight a stark contrast between single-threaded and multi-threaded performance. The server achieves top-tier single-core performance, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2351.0 and strong single-threaded metrics, such as 34.8 GB/sec in gzip compression. However, due to the low core count, multi-core performance is limited, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression falling into the weak category. Memory bandwidth also shows a divergence: cached small-block reads reach an average of 345.37 GB/sec, whereas uncached large-block reads and writes are relatively weak at 36.1 GB/sec and 25.44 GB/sec respectively.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the FX8-4ms_v2 offers a specialized hardware profile that prioritizes massive memory capacity over raw parallel compute power. This makes it highly efficient for workloads that are memory-bound rather than CPU-bound, avoiding the cost of provisioning excess CPU cores just to obtain high memory capacity. It is well-suited for memory-intensive database operations, in-memory caching layers, single-threaded data processing, and text processing tasks. Conversely, it is poorly suited for highly parallelized compute tasks, large-scale software compilation, or heavy LLM text generation, where its low core count presents clear performance tradeoffs.
